methods.name: Proposed
methods.note: Joint BS, relay, and RIS beamforming; the RIS supports both transmission phases.

methods.name: Random
methods.note: RIS phases are selected randomly; BS and relay beamforming are optimized for that configuration.

methods.name: Independent
methods.note: The RIS assists only phase I and is disabled in phase II. Beamforming is optimized for that setting.

methods.name: SingleRelay
methods.note: Relay-only system, with no RIS; BS and relay beamforming are optimized.

methods.name: DoubleRelay
methods.note: Replace the RIS with a second DF relay. Each relay receives half the available relay power for fairness.

plots.name: Topology 1
plots.caption: Figure 3 · Sum-rate versus RIS elements · (M, N, L, K) = (8, N, 4, 4). RIS at (100, 50) m.
plots.insight: Joint optimization of both transmission phases gives the proposed hybrid system the highest sum-rate in this reported sweep.

plots.name: Topology 2
plots.caption: Figure 7 · Sum-rate versus RIS elements · (8, N, 4, 4). RIS at (50, 50) m, closer to the BS.
plots.insight: Moving the RIS closer to the BS strengthens the first-phase contribution. Independent and Random improve relative to their Topology 1 results; placement changes the benchmark tradeoffs.

plots.name: Topology 3
plots.caption: Figure 9 · Sum-rate versus RIS elements · (8, N, 4, 4). RIS at (150, 50) m, farther from the BS.
plots.insight: The proposed joint design remains strong in this topology; Independent and Random have a smaller first-phase contribution.

plots.name: Imperfect CSI
plots.caption: Figure 11 · Topology 1 · perfect CSI and RIS–user error variances 0.001 and 0.01 · (8, N, 4, 4).
plots.insight: Channel-estimation error lowers performance. The proposed scheme remains stronger than Random under the same channel conditions; Independent is less affected because the RIS does not serve phase II.

plots.name: Convergence
plots.caption: Figure 12 · Sum-rate versus AO iteration · (M, N, L, K) = (8, 30, 8, K), K = 2, 4, 6, 8.
plots.insight: The reported curves converge in a few iterations. More users increase the number of BS beamforming subproblems; this does not establish real-time performance or global optimality.

plots.name: Energy efficiency
plots.caption: Figure 13 · Energy efficiency versus RIS elements · Topology 1 · (8, N, 4, 4). RIS power per element: 0.05 mW.
plots.insight: Additional RIS elements improve the reported energy efficiency more moderately than sum-rate because RIS power consumption also grows with the element count.
